subject.title: [Feature]: First-class multi-instance management for Docker installs

question: Should OpenClaw core own first-class `openclaw instance create/list/delete/update` lifecycle for Docker installs, or should multi-instance Docker remain documented profile/port/Compose/ClawDock primitives plus external helpers?
rationale: Current main has lower-level primitives, but an official lifecycle would add new persistent state, update, cleanup, port allocation, Compose naming, and security contracts that require maintainer product direction before implementation.

options.title: Design a minimal core lifecycle
options.body: Keep this issue open as the design anchor for a narrow lifecycle with explicit persistence, cleanup, update, port, Compose, and security semantics.

options.title: Keep manual primitives
options.body: Treat named profiles, unique ports, Compose, and ClawDock helpers as the supported Docker multi-instance workflow and close or redirect broader lifecycle requests later.

options.title: Prove externally first
options.body: Ask for a standalone or ClawHub-style helper package to prove the workflow before promoting any core CLI surface.

recommendation.title: Design a minimal core lifecycle
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the design anchor for a narrow lifecycle with explicit persistence, cleanup, update, port, Compose, and security semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest product-boundary signal among the likely owners, with recent multi-gateway registry work and adjacent Docker/sandbox changes.
